reference.label: Fibre break
reference.definition: A physical break in an optical fibre that prevents light from passing the break point.
reference.example: A cable cut between two sites removes all downstream optical light.

reference.label: Fibre-loss increase
reference.definition: An increase in fibre-span attenuation caused by bending, splicing, stress, or similar degradation.
reference.example: A severe bend adds 5 dB of span loss and lowers received power.

reference.label: Disconnected optical connection
reference.definition: An unplugged connector or patch cord that breaks optical continuity at a port or patch panel.
reference.example: A technician unplugs the patch cord feeding a preamplifier.

reference.label: Dirty optical connector
reference.definition: Connector contamination that introduces optical loss or reflections without fully breaking continuity.
reference.example: Dust on an LC connector adds loss and raises pre-FEC BER.

reference.label: Amplifier output failure
reference.definition: Failure of an amplifier pump or internal unit that leaves the amplifier with no usable optical output.
reference.example: An EDFA pump stops while input light remains present, making its output dark.

reference.label: Amplifier gain loss
reference.definition: A reduction of amplifier gain below its configured set point, weakening all carried channels.
reference.example: An amplifier configured for 20 dB gain provides only 16 dB.

reference.label: Amplifier noise increase
reference.definition: An increase in amplifier-added noise or noise figure that reduces channel OSNR.
reference.example: A deteriorating EDFA adds excess ASE noise while output power remains acceptable.

reference.label: Amplifier gain tilt
reference.definition: A non-flat amplifier gain profile that affects wavelengths unequally across the optical band.
reference.example: Long-wavelength edge channels receive 3 dB less gain than central channels.

reference.label: Pump ageing
reference.definition: Progressive pump deterioration evidenced by increasing drive current needed to maintain amplifier gain.
reference.example: Pump current rises from 100% to 116% of its beginning-of-life value.

reference.label: Transmit-laser failure
reference.definition: Failure of a line transmitter's laser that removes the optical channel launched toward the remote receiver.
reference.example: A transponder laser turns off and the far-end receiver loses its channel.

reference.label: Equipment-card failure
reference.definition: A complete internal card failure that removes its traffic and may invalidate or stop its monitoring.
reference.example: A line-card power-rail failure removes its channel and telemetry.

reference.label: Receiver degradation
reference.definition: A receiver-local deterioration that adds signal penalty without impairing the shared optical path.
reference.example: One coherent receiver becomes noisy while another receiver on the same path remains normal.

reference.label: Transmit-laser ageing
reference.definition: Progressive transmitter-laser ageing evidenced by an upward drift in required bias current.
reference.example: Laser bias rises by one percent per month while output remains serviceable.

reference.label: Channel-margin erosion
reference.definition: A slow decline in an optical channel's operating margin before complete service failure.
reference.example: A channel loses 0.2 dB of margin per week while traffic remains error-free.

reference.label: WSS attenuation drift
reference.definition: A change in a WSS channel-attenuation setting that leaves the selected channel at the wrong power.
reference.example: A WSS setting drifts from 3 dB to 7 dB and underpowers one channel.

reference.label: WSS passband shift
reference.definition: Frequency misalignment of a WSS passband with its carrier, imposing a filtering penalty that may leave power normal.
reference.example: A passband shifts away from a 193.1 THz carrier and raises pre-FEC errors.

reference.label: WSS input-port failure
reference.definition: Failure of a WSS input port that blocks channels entering through its associated ROADM degree.
reference.example: Failure of the west-degree input blocks every west-arriving wavelength.

reference.label: Blocked ROADM port
reference.definition: A ROADM port intentionally or erroneously held in a blocking state despite being required by the optical path.
reference.example: A newly provisioned add port remains blocked and the remote channel is absent.

reference.label: Differential-group-delay increase
reference.definition: An increase in optical-path DGD that can exceed coherent-receiver compensation tolerance.
reference.example: Changing fibre conditions increase DGD to 30 ps and cause intermittent frame loss.

reference.label: Fast polarization transient
reference.definition: A rapid state-of-polarization change that can exceed receiver tracking capability.
reference.example: An aerial-fibre disturbance rotates polarization too quickly for the receiver DSP.

reference.label: Mechanical fibre disturbance
reference.definition: A brief mechanical disturbance of fibre or patching that produces a transient optical-loss excursion.
reference.example: Movement of a patch panel causes a one-second power dip.

reference.label: Channel-loading transient
reference.definition: A brief multiplex-section power disturbance caused by adding or removing wavelength channels.
reference.example: Adding eight channels causes a short power swing while amplifiers re-equilibrate.

reference.label: Protection-switch interruption
reference.definition: A brief service interruption introduced while a protection selector changes paths.
reference.example: Traffic pauses for 30 ms while the selector moves to the protection ODU.

reference.label: OTN switch-fabric failure
reference.definition: Failure of an OTN cross-connect fabric that interrupts ODUs traversing the switch.
reference.example: A cross-connect ASIC failure stops every ODU routed through the switch.

reference.label: Wrong ODU cross-connection
reference.definition: An erroneous OTN cross-connect that delivers an ODU to a destination other than the provisioned one.
reference.example: Client A's ODU is connected to client C instead of client B.

reference.label: Client-port failure
reference.definition: Failure of a client-facing port or its optic that removes the associated client service.
reference.example: A failed 100GE pluggable takes down its client service.

reference.label: Instrument misreport
reference.definition: A monitoring fault in which an instrument reports an incorrect value rather than the actual physical state.
reference.example: A faulty power monitor reports −20 dBm while an external meter reads −5 dBm.

reference.label: Stale telemetry
reference.definition: A monitoring fault in which telemetry remains frozen and no longer reflects current conditions.
reference.example: Received-power telemetry stays at −6 dBm after the fibre is disconnected.

reference.label: Unspecified upstream failure
reference.definition: An unidentified failure somewhere upstream on the relevant signal path.
reference.example: A backward defect is attributed to an unknown remote failure.

reference.label: Unspecified server-layer failure
reference.definition: An unidentified failure in a lower or server layer on which an ODU path depends.
reference.example: An ODU fails because an unspecified supporting OTU or optical resource is unavailable.

reference.label: Optical signal loss
reference.definition: Absence of usable optical light, or power below the receiver's detection threshold.
reference.example: A line receiver sees power below detection after a fibre cut.

reference.label: Low optical power
reference.definition: Optical power below its expected operating level while some signal may still be present.
reference.example: A channel measures −12 dBm against a −3 dBm target.

reference.label: OSC loss
reference.definition: Loss of the optical supervisory channel on one fibre section, normally terminated at the next amplifier site.
reference.example: An ILA loses the upstream OSC while the following section generates its own OSC.

reference.label: Optical power excursion
reference.definition: A brief dip or swing in optical power lasting seconds or less.
reference.example: Channel loading produces a two-second 4 dB power dip.

reference.label: Low OSNR
reference.definition: Optical signal-to-noise ratio below its expected level because of added noise or lost signal margin.
reference.example: A channel retains nominal power but its OSNR falls from 21 dB to 17 dB.

reference.label: Polarization transient
reference.definition: A state-of-polarization variation fast enough to challenge or exceed receiver tracking.
reference.example: Rapid polarization rotation causes several errored seconds.

reference.label: High differential group delay
reference.definition: DGD elevated enough to impair coherent reception.
reference.example: The receiver estimates 30 ps DGD and intermittently loses framing.

reference.label: Optical filter penalty
reference.definition: Signal-quality degradation caused by spectral narrowing or passband misalignment, often without reduced measured power.
reference.example: A shifted WSS filter raises BER while channel power remains nominal.

reference.label: Receiver-local penalty
reference.definition: A quality penalty confined to one receiver that does not propagate along the optical path.
reference.example: Only one local receiver reports errors on an otherwise healthy channel.

reference.label: Unit down
reference.definition: A complete unit failure in which traffic is not carried and monitoring provides no valid current values.
reference.example: A failed line card loses traffic and stops updating telemetry.

reference.label: OTU frame loss
reference.definition: Loss of synchronization to OTU frame boundaries at a line receiver.
reference.example: Light is present at −4 dBm, but the receiver cannot identify OTU frames.

reference.label: OTU signal degradation
reference.definition: Pre-FEC errors above the configured degrade threshold while OTU frames remain aligned.
reference.example: Pre-FEC BER exceeds 1×10⁻³ and the OTU remains framed.

reference.label: ODU alarm indication signal
reference.definition: An Alarm Indication Signal carried downstream on an ODU to represent an upstream defect.
reference.example: An OTU frame loss causes ODU-AIS to reach the downstream client port.

reference.label: ODU misrouting
reference.definition: Delivery of an ODU to an endpoint other than its provisioned destination.
reference.example: A port expecting CLIENT-B receives the ODU identified as CLIENT-A.

reference.label: Client service down
reference.definition: Interruption of a client-facing service in at least one direction.
reference.example: Reception of ODU-AIS takes the 100GE client service down.

reference.label: Brief client-service hit
reference.definition: A short client-service interruption, typically during protection switching.
reference.example: The protected service pauses for 30 ms during path selection.

reference.label: Signal-quality degradation
reference.definition: Reduced signal integrity or margin while the signal remains present.
reference.example: A channel develops rising pre-FEC BER despite normal received power.

reference.label: Normal optical power
reference.definition: Optical power within its expected range, including cases where another non-power impairment exists.
reference.example: The channel remains at −3 dBm while a filter penalty raises BER.

reference.label: Node power re-leveling
reference.definition: Restoration of an incoming channel to configured output power by node equalization.
reference.example: A channel arriving 4 dB low leaves the ROADM at its nominal target.

reference.label: Residual OSNR penalty after re-leveling
reference.definition: An OSNR degradation that remains after node equalization has restored nominal optical power.
reference.example: The ROADM restores −2 dBm output power, but OSNR remains 4 dB below baseline.

reference.label: Traffic-alarm masking
reference.definition: Suppression of dependent traffic alarms because a higher-level equipment alarm is active.
reference.example: A card-failure alarm hides derived OTU frame-loss alarms on that card.

reference.label: Backward defect indication
reference.definition: A backward indication reporting that the remote receiver detected a defect on the transmitted signal.
reference.example: A receiver that loses OTU framing returns BDI toward the transmitter.

reference.label: Protection path active
reference.definition: A protection state in which client traffic is currently carried over the configured protection ODU path.
reference.example: After the working path fails, the selector forwards traffic over the backup route.

reference.label: Protection path unavailable
reference.definition: A state in which the configured protection path is defective and cannot provide reliable backup.
reference.example: Loss of framing on the standby ODU makes protection unavailable.

reference.label: Per-channel optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured separately for an individual wavelength channel.
reference.example: A ROADM channel monitor reports −3.1 dBm at 193.1 THz.

reference.label: Per-channel OSNR
reference.definition: Optical signal-to-noise ratio measured separately for an individual wavelength channel.
reference.example: The channel monitor reports 21 dB OSNR for one wavelength.

reference.label: Received optical power
reference.definition: Optical power measured at a line receiver.
reference.example: A coherent line interface reports received power of −6.2 dBm.

reference.label: Received-power PM15
reference.definition: Received optical-power statistics accumulated in 15-minute performance intervals.
reference.example: The 10:00–10:15 bin records an average received power of −6.4 dBm.

reference.label: Line errored seconds PM15
reference.definition: The count of line-interface seconds containing errors within a 15-minute performance interval.
reference.example: The terminal reports 12 errored seconds for the latest 15-minute bin.

reference.label: Estimated OSNR
reference.definition: An OSNR estimate derived by a coherent receiver or its DSP.
reference.example: Receiver telemetry estimates the channel OSNR at 18.7 dB.

reference.label: Pre-FEC bit error ratio
reference.definition: The ratio of erroneous received bits before forward-error correction is applied.
reference.example: The line receiver reports a pre-FEC BER of 8×10⁻⁴.

reference.label: Differential group delay
reference.definition: The measured delay difference between the principal polarization modes of an optical signal.
reference.example: The coherent receiver reports 18 ps of DGD.

reference.label: Polarization-change rate
reference.definition: The measured rate of change of the received signal's state of polarization.
reference.example: DSP telemetry shows a polarization rate above its tracking threshold.

reference.label: Amplifier input power
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power measured at an amplifier input.
reference.example: An inline amplifier reports −8 dBm total input power.

reference.label: Amplifier output power
reference.definition: Aggregate optical power measured at an amplifier output.
reference.example: A booster reports +17 dBm total output power.

reference.label: Pump-current percentage
reference.definition: Amplifier pump drive current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: A five-year-old amplifier reports pump current at 116%.

reference.label: Laser-bias percentage
reference.definition: Transmitter-laser bias current expressed as a percentage of its beginning-of-life value.
reference.example: A transmitter reports laser bias at 109% of beginning-of-life current.

reference.label: Client errored seconds PM15
reference.definition: The count of client-interface seconds containing errors within a 15-minute interval.
reference.example: A 100GE port reports three client errored seconds from 12:00 to 12:15.

reference.label: Client unavailable seconds PM15
reference.definition: The count of seconds for which a client interface was unavailable within a 15-minute interval.
reference.example: A failed optic produces 900 unavailable seconds in one full bin.

reference.label: Alarm-only monitor
reference.definition: A monitor whose state is exposed through alarms rather than reported numerical values.
reference.example: An OSC receiver raises loss alarms but exposes no received-power value.

reference.label: Optical amplifier
reference.definition: A line-system device that amplifies an optical multiplexed signal.
reference.example: An EDFA restores WDM power after a long fibre span.

reference.label: Booster amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier at the transmitting end of an optical multiplex section, after the ROADM.
reference.example: A booster raises ROADM output power before the outgoing fibre span.

reference.label: Inline amplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier at an intermediate site along an optical multiplex section.
reference.example: An ILA amplifies the WDM signal at a midpoint hut.

reference.label: Preamplifier
reference.definition: An optical amplifier at the receiving end of an optical multiplex section, before the ROADM.
reference.example: A preamplifier raises incoming span power before receive-side switching.

reference.label: Coherent line interface
reference.definition: A coherent optical interface that transmits or terminates one line-side optical channel.
reference.example: A 400G coherent interface terminates the lightpath at site B.

reference.label: Transponder
reference.definition: A terminal resource that maps a client signal to and from a line-side optical channel.
reference.example: A transponder maps one 400GE client onto a coherent wavelength.

reference.label: Muxponder
reference.definition: A terminal resource that combines multiple lower-rate clients into a higher-rate line signal.
reference.example: A muxponder combines four 100GE clients into one 400G channel.

reference.label: OTN line card
reference.definition: A card that terminates OTN line signals and exposes their ODUs for switching or client mapping.
reference.example: An OTN line card terminates an OTU and presents its ODUs to the fabric.

reference.label: ROADM
reference.definition: A wavelength-routing node using WSS functions to add, drop, and direct optical channels.
reference.example: A ROADM routes 193.1 THz from the west degree to the east degree.

reference.label: Colourless directionless contentionless ROADM
reference.definition: A ROADM able to add or drop wavelengths without fixed colour, direction, or contention restrictions.
reference.example: A CDC node assigns equal-frequency services to different add/drop resources.

reference.label: OTN switch
reference.definition: Equipment that cross-connects ODUs through an internal switching fabric.
reference.example: An OTN switch maps an incoming ODU2 to a 100GE client port.

reference.label: ODU cross-connect fabric
reference.definition: The internal OTN forwarding fabric that establishes ODU cross-connections.
reference.example: The fabric connects an ODU from line-card port 1 to client port 8.

reference.label: Client port
reference.definition: A client-facing port that maps a client signal into or out of an ODU.
reference.example: A 100GE client port maps a customer service into an ODU.

reference.label: One optical channel
reference.definition: A single optical wavelength channel rather than the whole multiplexed signal.
reference.example: A WSS passband shift affects only the 193.1 THz channel.

reference.label: All optical channels
reference.definition: Every wavelength channel in the referenced multiplexed signal or resource.
reference.example: A dark line-amplifier output removes all 80 carried channels.

reference.label: Some optical channels
reference.definition: A proper subset of the multiplexed channels rather than the entire set.
reference.example: Gain tilt weakens five edge channels while the others remain normal.

reference.label: ROADM degree input
reference.definition: Every channel entering a ROADM through one degree's WSS input port.
reference.example: A west-input failure blocks every wavelength arriving on the west degree.

reference.label: One receiver
reference.definition: The specific receiver under observation, excluding the shared path and other receivers.
reference.example: Errors appear at this receiver while another receiver remains normal.

reference.label: Equipment unit
reference.definition: The complete managed equipment unit rather than an individual channel or its traffic.
reference.example: A pump-health indicator applies to the whole amplifier unit.

reference.label: Every ODU through a switch
reference.definition: All ODU cross-connections whose routes traverse a specified OTN switch.
reference.example: A fabric failure interrupts every ODU cross-connected through the switch.

reference.label: One ODU
reference.definition: A single ODU connection rather than all ODUs carried by a switch or line signal.
reference.example: A bad cross-connect misroutes one ODU while unrelated ODUs remain correct.

reference.label: Client service
reference.definition: The customer-facing service carried through a client port and its associated ODU path.
reference.example: The protected 100GE connection is the client service being monitored.

reference.label: Current unit
reference.definition: The managed equipment instance that raised the alarm or observed the condition.
reference.example: For a gain alarm on ILA-7, the current unit is ILA-7.

reference.label: Current port
reference.definition: The specific local port that raised or reports the condition.
reference.example: For a port-hardware alarm on 1/4, the current port is client port 1/4.

reference.label: Upstream fibre span
reference.definition: The fibre span immediately preceding and feeding the current unit.
reference.example: The span from ILA-1 to ILA-2 is ILA-2's upstream span.

reference.label: Immediately upstream amplifier
reference.definition: The nearest amplifier whose output feeds the span or unit under observation.
reference.example: ILA-1 is the immediately upstream amplifier for ILA-2.

reference.label: Optical multiplex-section input
reference.definition: The patch or ingress connection where the composite optical signal enters an OMS.
reference.example: The patch between the ROADM and booster is the OMS input.

reference.label: Upstream ROADM channel point
reference.definition: The relevant channel or WSS input at the immediately preceding ROADM on the signal path.
reference.example: The 193.1 THz west-degree WSS input is the upstream ROADM channel point.

reference.label: Upstream optical path
reference.definition: Any preceding fibre, amplifier, patch, or ROADM resource on the optical signal's route.
reference.example: A dirty connector two sites earlier lies upstream on the affected channel path.

reference.label: Far-end transmitter
reference.definition: The remote line interface transmitting the optical signal received by the current unit.
reference.example: For the receiver at site B, the far-end transmitter is at site A.

reference.label: Far-end receiver
reference.definition: The remote line interface receiving the optical signal transmitted by the current unit.
reference.example: A failed local laser causes signal loss at the far-end receiver.

reference.label: Path to the far end
reference.definition: The end-to-end signal route between the current endpoint and its remote peer.
reference.example: The path includes terminal interfaces, ROADMs, amplifiers, fibre, and patching.

reference.label: Either client endpoint
reference.definition: Either of the two client-facing ports terminating a service.
reference.example: Failure of the client optic at site A or site B is at either endpoint.

reference.label: OTN switch on ODU path
reference.definition: An OTN switch or cross-connect lying on the end-to-end route of an ODU.
reference.example: A misconnection in the intermediate switch lies on the service's ODU path.

reference.label: Working ODU path
reference.definition: The primary ODU route normally selected to carry a protected service.
reference.example: The direct A–B route is the working ODU path.

reference.label: Protection ODU path
reference.definition: The alternate ODU route intended to carry a service when the working route is defective.
reference.example: The diverse A–C–B route is the protection ODU path.

reference.label: Active ODU path
reference.definition: The working or protection ODU route currently carrying live client traffic.
reference.example: After protection switching, the backup route becomes the active ODU path.

reference.label: Baseline monitoring
reference.definition: Alarms and interval performance counters available as standard monitoring.
reference.example: Every line interface reports alarms and 15-minute errored-second counters.

reference.label: Power monitoring
reference.definition: Optional monitoring that exposes optical input, output, or received-power values.
reference.example: A power-enabled amplifier reports total input and output power.

reference.label: Optical channel monitoring
reference.definition: Monitoring that exposes per-channel power and OSNR at a ROADM degree.
reference.example: An equipped ROADM reports power and OSNR for each wavelength.

reference.label: Advanced coherent monitoring
reference.definition: Monitoring that exposes coherent-DSP quantities and equipment-health currents.
reference.example: An advanced interface reports pre-FEC BER, DGD, OSNR, and polarization rate.

reference.label: Hard failure
reference.definition: An abrupt and complete functional loss that interrupts affected traffic.
reference.example: A stopped amplifier pump makes the output dark and drops all channels.

reference.label: Soft degradation
reference.definition: Reduced signal quality or margin while traffic remains at least partly available.
reference.example: A 3 dB OSNR decline raises errors without immediately stopping traffic.

reference.label: Incipient degradation
reference.definition: A slow pre-failure trend that has not yet materially affected traffic.
reference.example: Pump current rises for months while configured gain is still maintained.

reference.label: Transient event
reference.definition: A brief event, normally lasting seconds or less rather than persisting.
reference.example: A mechanical disturbance produces a one-second optical-power dip.

reference.label: Critical severity
reference.definition: The highest operational alarm severity for serious service or equipment impact.
reference.example: A switch-fabric failure interrupting all ODUs is classified critical.

reference.label: Major severity
reference.definition: A high alarm severity indicating significant loss or degradation requiring prompt action.
reference.example: Loss of an unprotected client service is classified major.

reference.label: Minor severity
reference.definition: A low alarm severity for a condition needing attention without major current service impact.
reference.example: An early pump-ageing warning with unaffected traffic is classified minor.

reference.label: Not alarmed
reference.definition: A reported condition that does not currently generate an active alarm.
reference.example: A small pump-current increase within normal limits is reported but not alarmed.

reference.label: Pass condition unchanged
reference.definition: Forward an arriving condition without correcting or materially altering it.
reference.example: A DGD impairment passes through an intermediate ROADM unchanged.

reference.label: Per-channel ROADM routing
reference.definition: Independent switching of each wavelength so a line-wide condition continues on each routed channel.
reference.example: One wavelength is routed east while another is dropped locally.

reference.label: OTU frame-loss consequent actions
reference.definition: On OTU frame loss, insert ODU-AIS downstream and send BDI toward the remote transmitter.
reference.example: A line card losing OTU framing sends AIS to mapped clients and BDI upstream.

reference.label: ODU-AIS forwarding
reference.definition: Propagation of an incoming ODU-AIS through each affected ODU cross-connection.
reference.example: An OTN switch forwards received AIS to the corresponding egress ODUs.

reference.label: Optical-channel loss-of-signal alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that no usable optical-channel light reaches the line receiver.
reference.example: A fibre cut removes channel light and the terminal raises OCH_LOS.

reference.label: OTU loss-of-frame alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating loss of OTU frame alignment, commonly while optical light remains present.
reference.example: Excess DGD prevents framing and the receiver raises OTU_LOF.

reference.label: OTU signal-degrade alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that pre-FEC errors have exceeded the configured degrade threshold.
reference.example: A dirty connector raises BER above threshold and triggers OTU_SD.

reference.label: OTU backward-defect alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that the far end reports a defect on the locally transmitted OTU signal.
reference.example: The local terminal raises OTU_BDI after the remote receiver loses framing.

reference.label: Transmit-equipment failure alarm
reference.definition: An equipment alarm indicating a locally detected transmit-laser or laser-drive fault.
reference.example: Missing laser output causes the transponder to raise EQPT_TX_FAIL.

reference.label: Card-equipment failure alarm
reference.definition: An equipment alarm indicating an internal hardware failure of a card.
reference.example: A failed FPGA causes the line card to raise EQPT_CARD_FAIL.

reference.label: Amplifier input-loss alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that no usable optical light reaches a line amplifier's input.
reference.example: A broken upstream span causes an inline amplifier to raise AMP_INPUT_LOS.

reference.label: OMS loss-of-signal alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating loss of multiplexed optical light at a receiving-end OMS input.
reference.example: A disconnected receive patch cord causes the preamplifier to raise OMS_LOS_P.

reference.label: OSC loss alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that the optical supervisory channel is not received from the feeding section.
reference.example: An ILA missing its upstream supervisory carrier raises OSC_LOS.

reference.label: Amplifier failure alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating amplifier input light is present but no usable output is produced.
reference.example: Normal input with a dark output after pump failure triggers AMP_FAIL.

reference.label: Amplifier gain-out-of-range alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that actual amplifier gain differs excessively from its configured set point.
reference.example: A 20 dB target measuring 17 dB triggers AMP_GAIN_OOR.

reference.label: Amplifier pump end-of-life alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that pump drive current has crossed the configured end-of-life threshold.
reference.example: Pump current reaching 123% of beginning-of-life value triggers AMP_PUMP_EOL.

reference.label: Client service-failure alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that the client-facing service is unavailable.
reference.example: A failed client optic takes down the service and raises CLIENT_SF.

reference.label: ODU-AIS receive alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that an ODU Alarm Indication Signal has been received at the monitored endpoint.
reference.example: An egress client port detects downstream ODU-AIS and raises ODU_AIS.

reference.label: ODU backward-defect alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that the far end reports receiving an ODU defect or AIS.
reference.example: The remote endpoint reports incoming AIS and the local port raises ODU_BDI.

reference.label: ODU trail-trace mismatch alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that the received ODU trail identifier differs from the provisioned expectation.
reference.example: A port expecting trace CLIENT-B receives CLIENT-A and raises ODU_TIM.

reference.label: Protection-active indication
reference.definition: A status indication that a protected client service is currently using its protection path.
reference.example: After the working ODU fails, the selector switches and reports PROT_ACTIVE.

reference.label: Protection-unavailable alarm
reference.definition: An alarm indicating that the configured protection path has failed or is unavailable.
reference.example: Loss of framing on the standby ODU triggers PROT_UNAVAIL.

reference.label: Port-equipment failure alarm
reference.definition: An equipment alarm indicating an internal hardware fault in a client port.
reference.example: A failed Ethernet PHY causes the client port to raise EQPT_PORT_FAIL.

reference.label: OTN fabric failure alarm
reference.definition: An equipment alarm indicating a hardware or functional fault in an OTN cross-connect fabric.
reference.example: A failed fabric ASIC causes the OTN switch to raise OTN_FABRIC_FAIL.
